title: 166,000 people could unlock your phone
description:
Apple says the chance a random person's finger unlocks Touch ID is 1 in 50,000 (one enrolled finger), so across 8.3 billion people about 166,000 fingers would pass. The phone stores no image, only a mathematical map of your ridges, and every touch is scored against it; because no touch is perfect, the bar is set so about 1 stranger in 50,000 clears it. What keeps you safe is the limit: after 5 failed tries it asks for the passcode, so a thief with random fingers has about a 1 in 10,000 chance, the same as guessing a 4-digit PIN once. Face ID sets the bar at less than 1 in 1,000,000: about 8,300 people, 1 in 200,000 over 5 tries (higher odds for twins, look-alike siblings and children under 13).

Numbers checked in code, with 2,000,000 simulated thieves. Sources: Apple Support, About Touch ID advanced security technology; Apple Support, About Face ID advanced technology; UN World Population Prospects 2024 (8.3 billion in 2026).

social_caption: About 166,000 people on Earth have a finger that would unlock your phone. Here's the math, and the one number that keeps you safe anyway.
facts_checked: Touch ID: the probability a random person could unlock with their fingerprint is 1 in 50,000 with a single enrolled finger; 5 unsuccessful attempts before the password is required; no fingerprint images stored, only a mathematical representation (https://support.apple.com/en-us/105095)

Face ID: less than 1 in 1,000,000 with a single enrolled appearance; 5 unsuccessful attempts before a passcode is required; higher for twins, look-alike siblings and children under 13 (https://support.apple.com/en-us/102381)
World population mid-2026 about 8.3 billion (UN World Population Prospects 2024, via https://statisticstimes.com/demographics/world-population.php)

beats.say: Not hackers. Not copies. Just strangers whose finger happens to pass.
Your phone's maker says a random finger gets in one time in 50,000.
Your phone never keeps a picture of your print. It keeps a map of your ridges, and scores every touch against it.
No touch is perfect, so it can't demand a perfect score. It sets a bar, and one stranger in 50,000 clears it.
Now take 8.3 billion people, divide by 50,000. That's 166,000.
So why is your phone safe? One more number. 5.
After 5 misses, it wants your passcode. So a thief gets one chance in 10,000, like guessing a 4-digit PIN once.
Face unlock sets the bar 20 times higher. One in a million. About 8,300 faces.
166,000 people could open your phone. A thief just gets 5 tries to find one.
